{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_019hXgeQLmdrtAp6SqPEDUfK","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# Theoria Medical, PLLC — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-15\n     4→Developer website: https://theoriamedical.com/\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→Theoria Medical is a tech-enabled medical group and technology company founded in 2019, headquartered in Novi, Michigan. The company provides primary care physician services to senior living communities — including skilled nursing facilities (SNFs), assisted living facilities, continuing care retirement communities, and independent living communities — across 21 states. Theoria is not a traditional EHR vendor selling software to outside customers; rather, it is a physician group practice that built its own proprietary EHR (ChartEasy) for internal use by its own clinicians. The company employs physicians, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants who provide on-site rounding, telemedicine, medical directorship, chronic care management (CCM), and remote patient monitoring (RPM) at partner facilities.\n     9→\n    10→Theoria operates as a value-based care organization, having joined the ACO REACH (High Needs) program through a partnership with Empassion Health in January 2024. In December 2024, Amulet Capital Partners invested in Theoria Management (the management services organization arm). The company has grown rapidly — employee estimates range from ~200 to 1,000+ depending on the source and timing, reflecting significant recent expansion. Theoria serves \"hundreds\" of senior living and care residential locations across 21 states, per press coverage. CEO Kevin Murphy leads the organization.\n    11→\n    12→Critically, ChartEasy is purpose-built for Theoria's own clinicians — it is not sold as a commercial EHR product to external healthcare organizations. The facilities where Theoria physicians provide care typically use their own facility EHR systems (PointClickCare, MatrixCare, American HealthTech), and ChartEasy integrates bidirectionally with those systems.\n    13→\n    14→## Product: ChartEasy\n    15→\n    16→CHPL IDs: 11542\n    17→\n    18→### What It Is\n    19→\n    20→ChartEasy is an ONC-certified, cloud-based electronic health record developed by Theoria Medical specifically for the long-term care (LTC) and post-acute care settings. It is a physician-facing EHR — used by Theoria's own physicians, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants who provide care in SNFs and other senior living communities. The product is supported on web and iOS platforms.\n    21→\n    22→ChartEasy is the certified Health IT Module, but it exists within a broader ecosystem of Theoria proprietary technology tools:\n    23→- **ChartEasy** — the EHR for clinical documentation, orders, medication management\n    24→- **ChatEasy** — secure clinical messaging platform for communication between LTC facility care teams and Theoria's medical staff\n    25→- **ProphEasy** — AI/ML clinical decision support tool for predicting return-to-hospitalization (RTH) risk\n    26→- **Theoria Telemedicine** — virtual care delivery platform\n    27→- **Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM)** — continuous vital sign monitoring with devices and automated alerts\n    28→\n    29→The certified module (ChartEasy v1.5) has a broad certification profile with 34 criteria and 10 Clinical Quality Measures. The SED intended user description is \"Ambulatory/Post-Acute.\"\n    30→\n    31→### Users & Market\n    32→\n    33→**Primary users**: Theoria Medical's own clinicians — physicians, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants — who provide attending physician services, medical directorship, and telemedicine at partner senior living facilities.\n    34→\n    35→**Clinical settings**: Skilled nursing facilities, assisted living, continuing care retirement communities, independent living, and home health. The patient population is primarily elderly, high-acuity, Medicare-eligible residents in institutional settings.\n    36→\n    37→**Scale**: Theoria serves \"hundreds\" of senior living locations across 21 states. The company has been growing rapidly.\n    38→\n    39→**Key distinction**: ChartEasy is an internal-use EHR. It is not sold to external customers. The facilities where Theoria's clinicians work have their own EHR systems (typically PointClickCare or MatrixCare); ChartEasy serves as the physician's EHR that integrates with the facility's system.\n    40→\n    41→### Modules & Functionality\n    42→\n    43→Based on vendor website, product pages, partner marketplace listings, and App Store descriptions:\n    44→\n    45→**Clinical Documentation**\n    46→- Physician progress notes and encounter documentation for SNF visits\n    47→- Notes are delivered instantaneously to facility EHR (e.g., MatrixCare, PointClickCare) upon signature\n    48→- Signed encounters viewable in patient portal (per App Store listing, added v2.0.4)\n    49→\n    50→**Medication Management**\n    51→- Automated medication reconciliation algorithm\n    52→- Support for polypharmacy management and gradual dose reduction (GDR) — both specific to the SNF regulatory environment\n    53→- Current medication lists accessible via patient portal\n    54→- The system is certified for (a)(1) CPOE and (a)(4) drug-drug/drug-allergy interaction checks, and (a)(14) implantable device list, indicating it handles ordering workflows\n    55→\n    56→**Scheduling**\n    57→- Automated patient scheduling algorithm that adheres to regulatory guidelines (likely CMS-required physician visit frequencies for SNF residents)\n    58→\n    59→**Lab & Imaging**\n    60→- Integration with laboratory and imaging companies\n    61→- Real-time access to lab results (confirmed on patient portal and product page)\n    62→- Lab data exchange is bidirectional\n    63→\n    64→**Clinical Decision Support**\n    65→- ProphEasy AI tool for return-to-hospitalization prediction\n    66→- Diagnosis-specific vital range alerts\n    67→- The system is certified for (a)(5) clinical decision support\n    68→\n    69→**Remote Patient Monitoring**\n    70→- Two device options for facilities\n    71→- Monitors: heart rate, respiration rate, motion, presence, blood oxygen saturation\n    72→- Real-time vitals pushed to ChartEasy and facility EHR\n    73→- Abnormality alerts triggered via diagnosis-specific vital ranges\n    74→- Alerts delivered through ChartEasy and ChatEasy messaging\n    75→\n    76→**Chronic Care Management (CCM)**\n    77→- Individualized care plans accessible via patient portal\n    78→- CCM module for managing chronic conditions in the SNF population\n    79→\n    80→**Secure Messaging (ChatEasy)**\n    81→- Multi-channel instant messaging between medical staff and facility care teams\n    82→- Nursing receives alerts with abnormal vitals via ChatEasy\n    83→- Real-time communication for care coordination\n    84→\n    85→**Telemedicine**\n    86→- Virtual care delivery infrastructure (Theoria Telemedicine platform)\n    87→- Supports remote clinical encounters\n    88→\n    89→**Patient Portal**\n    90→- ChartEasy Patient Portal (web and iOS app)\n    91→- View lab results and vital signs\n    92→- View current medications\n    93→- View signed clinical encounters\n    94→- Access CCM care plans\n    95→- Download and transmit health records (PDF and CCDA formats)\n    96→- Share health information with authorized representatives and other providers\n    97→\n    98→**Interoperability & Integrations**\n    99→- Bidirectional integration with PointClickCare (demographics, ADT, medications, vitals, diagnoses flow in; physician notes flow out)\n   100→- Bidirectional integration with MatrixCare (same pattern)\n   101→- Integration with American HealthTech\n   102→- Hospital EMR system integrations\n   103→- Laboratory and imaging company integrations\n   104→- Certified for (b)(1) transitions of care, (b)(2) clinical information reconciliation\n   105→- Certified for (g)(7)-(g)(10) FHIR/API access\n   106→- Certified for (e)(1) view/download/transmit, (e)(3) patient health information export\n   107→- Certified for (h)(1) direct project messaging\n   108→\n   109→**Regulatory Compliance**\n   110→- Designed to align with LTC regulatory requirements (CMS conditions of participation, MDS-related workflows)\n   111→- Clinical Quality Measures (10 CQMs certified)\n   112→\n   113→**Supported Terminologies** (per Medigy listing)\n   114→- ICD-9, ICD-10, SNOMED CT, LOINC, NDC, RxNorm, CPT, HCPCS, RadLex, MEDCIN\n   115→\n   116→### Data & Content\n   117→\n   118→Based on the evidence gathered, ChartEasy stores or manages the following types of data:\n   119→\n   120→**Clinical data confirmed by product documentation:**\n   121→- Patient demographics (received from facility EHR integrations)\n   122→- ADT (admission/discharge/transfer) records (from facility integrations)\n   123→- Physician progress notes and encounter documentation\n   124→- Medication lists and reconciliation data\n   125→- Vital signs (both manual and from RPM devices)\n   126→- Lab results (from laboratory integrations)\n   127→- Diagnoses (received from facility EHR, also managed internally)\n   128→- Implantable device information (implied by (a)(14) certification)\n   129→- Clinical decision support alerts and risk predictions (ProphEasy RTH scores)\n   130→- Care plans (CCM care plans, accessible via portal)\n   131→- Scheduling data (visit scheduling per regulatory requirements)\n   132→- Patient portal access logs and patient-generated data\n   133→\n   134→**Clinical messaging data:**\n   135→- ChatEasy secure messages between Theoria clinicians and facility nursing staff\n   136→- Alert notifications for abnormal vitals\n   137→\n   138→**RPM device data:**\n   139→- Heart rate, respiration rate, motion, presence, blood oxygen saturation readings\n   140→- Continuous monitoring streams from RPM devices\n   141→\n   142→**What is unclear or not mentioned:**\n   143→- **Billing/claims**: The website does not explicitly describe billing or claims management functionality within ChartEasy. However, CPT and HCPCS terminologies are listed as supported, and Theoria operates as a physician group that bills Medicare (fee-for-service and value-based). It is unclear whether billing is handled within ChartEasy or through a separate billing system.\n   144→- **E-prescribing**: Despite medication management being a core feature, explicit e-prescribing (Surescripts integration) is not mentioned on the website. However, (a)(1) CPOE certification and RxNorm/NDC terminology support suggest prescribing workflows exist.\n   145→- **Imaging results**: Integration with \"imaging companies\" is mentioned but details are sparse.\n   146→- **Referral management**: Not described.\n   147→- **Quality reporting/MDS data**: While regulatory compliance is emphasized and CQMs are certified, explicit MDS (Minimum Data Set) data management is not described — MDS is typically the facility's responsibility, not the attending physician's.\n   148→- **Historical claims data**: Theoria references having \"historical claims data\" for ACO REACH analytics, but it's unclear if this is stored in ChartEasy or a separate analytics platform.\n   149→\n   150→---\n   151→\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. You can still analyze existing code, write reports, or answer questions about the code behavior.\n</system-reminder>\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"0a684cb1-23e0-4dc9-b119-21c3f9eca41e","uuid":"5029eeef-4293-4b3a-bb1d-a081cb4c4f04","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/theoria-medical-pllc--charteasy/product-research.md","content":"# Theoria Medical, PLLC — Product Research\n\nResearched: 2026-02-15\nDeveloper website: https://theoriamedical.com/\n\n## Overview\n\nTheoria Medical is a tech-enabled medical group and technology company founded in 2019, headquartered in Novi, Michigan. The company provides primary care physician services to senior living communities — including skilled nursing facilities (SNFs), assisted living facilities, continuing care retirement communities, and independent living communities — across 21 states. Theoria is not a traditional EHR vendor selling software to outside customers; rather, it is a physician group practice that built its own proprietary EHR (ChartEasy) for internal use by its own clinicians. The company employs physicians, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants who provide on-site rounding, telemedicine, medical directorship, chronic care management (CCM), and remote patient monitoring (RPM) at partner facilities.\n\nTheoria operates as a value-based care organization, having joined the ACO REACH (High Needs) program through a partnership with Empassion Health in January 2024. In December 2024, Amulet Capital Partners invested in Theoria Management (the management services organization arm). The company has grown rapidly — employee estimates range from ~200 to 1,000+ depending on the source and timing, reflecting significant recent expansion. Theoria serves \"hundreds\" of senior living and care residential locations across 21 states, per press coverage. CEO Kevin Murphy leads the organization.\n\nCritically, ChartEasy is purpose-built for Theoria's own clinicians — it is not sold as a commercial EHR product to external healthcare organizations. The facilities where Theoria physicians provide care typically use their own facility EHR systems (PointClickCare, MatrixCare, American HealthTech), and ChartEasy integrates bidirectionally with those systems.\n\n## Product: ChartEasy\n\nCHPL IDs: 11542\n\n### What It Is\n\nChartEasy is an ONC-certified, cloud-based electronic health record developed by Theoria Medical specifically for the long-term care (LTC) and post-acute care settings. It is a physician-facing EHR — used by Theoria's own physicians, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants who provide care in SNFs and other senior living communities. The product is supported on web and iOS platforms.\n\nChartEasy is the certified Health IT Module, but it exists within a broader ecosystem of Theoria proprietary technology tools:\n- **ChartEasy** — the EHR for clinical documentation, orders, medication management\n- **ChatEasy** — secure clinical messaging platform for communication between LTC facility care teams and Theoria's medical staff\n- **ProphEasy** — AI/ML clinical decision support tool for predicting return-to-hospitalization (RTH) risk\n- **Theoria Telemedicine** — virtual care delivery platform\n- **Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM)** — continuous vital sign monitoring with devices and automated alerts\n\nThe certified module (ChartEasy v1.5) has a broad certification profile with 34 criteria and 10 Clinical Quality Measures. The SED intended user description is \"Ambulatory/Post-Acute.\"\n\n### Users & Market\n\n**Primary users**: Theoria Medical's own clinicians — physicians, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants — who provide attending physician services, medical directorship, and telemedicine at partner senior living facilities.\n\n**Clinical settings**: Skilled nursing facilities, assisted living, continuing care retirement communities, independent living, and home health. The patient population is primarily elderly, high-acuity, Medicare-eligible residents in institutional settings.\n\n**Scale**: Theoria serves \"hundreds\" of senior living locations across 21 states. The company has been growing rapidly.\n\n**Key distinction**: ChartEasy is an internal-use EHR. It is not sold to external customers. The facilities where Theoria's clinicians work have their own EHR systems (typically PointClickCare or MatrixCare); ChartEasy serves as the physician's EHR that integrates with the facility's system.\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nBased on vendor website, product pages, partner marketplace listings, and App Store descriptions:\n\n**Clinical Documentation**\n- Physician progress notes and encounter documentation for SNF visits\n- Notes are delivered instantaneously to facility EHR (e.g., MatrixCare, PointClickCare) upon signature\n- Signed encounters viewable in patient portal (per App Store listing, added v2.0.4)\n\n**Medication Management**\n- Automated medication reconciliation algorithm\n- Support for polypharmacy management and gradual dose reduction (GDR) — both specific to the SNF regulatory environment\n- Current medication lists accessible via patient portal\n- The system is certified for (a)(1) CPOE and (a)(4) drug-drug/drug-allergy interaction checks, and (a)(14) implantable device list, indicating it handles ordering workflows\n\n**Scheduling**\n- Automated patient scheduling algorithm that adheres to regulatory guidelines (likely CMS-required physician visit frequencies for SNF residents)\n\n**Lab & Imaging**\n- Integration with laboratory and imaging companies\n- Real-time access to lab results (confirmed on patient portal and product page)\n- Lab data exchange is bidirectional\n\n**Clinical Decision Support**\n- ProphEasy AI tool for return-to-hospitalization prediction\n- Diagnosis-specific vital range alerts\n- The system is certified for (a)(5) clinical decision support\n\n**Remote Patient Monitoring**\n- Two device options for facilities\n- Monitors: heart rate, respiration rate, motion, presence, blood oxygen saturation\n- Real-time vitals pushed to ChartEasy and facility EHR\n- Abnormality alerts triggered via diagnosis-specific vital ranges\n- Alerts delivered through ChartEasy and ChatEasy messaging\n\n**Chronic Care Management (CCM)**\n- Individualized care plans accessible via patient portal\n- CCM module for managing chronic conditions in the SNF population\n\n**Secure Messaging (ChatEasy)**\n- Multi-channel instant messaging between medical staff and facility care teams\n- Nursing receives alerts with abnormal vitals via ChatEasy\n- Real-time communication for care coordination\n\n**Telemedicine**\n- Virtual care delivery infrastructure (Theoria Telemedicine platform)\n- Supports remote clinical encounters\n\n**Patient Portal**\n- ChartEasy Patient Portal (web and iOS app)\n- View lab results and vital signs\n- View current medications\n- View signed clinical encounters\n- Access CCM care plans\n- Download and transmit health records (PDF and CCDA formats)\n- Share health information with authorized representatives and other providers\n\n**Interoperability & Integrations**\n- Bidirectional integration with PointClickCare (demographics, ADT, medications, vitals, diagnoses flow in; physician notes flow out)\n- Bidirectional integration with MatrixCare (same pattern)\n- Integration with American HealthTech\n- Hospital EMR system integrations\n- Laboratory and imaging company integrations\n- Certified for (b)(1) transitions of care, (b)(2) clinical information reconciliation\n- Certified for (g)(7)-(g)(10) FHIR/API access\n- Certified for (e)(1) view/download/transmit, (e)(3) patient health information export\n- Certified for (h)(1) direct project messaging\n\n**Regulatory Compliance**\n- Designed to align with LTC regulatory requirements (CMS conditions of participation, MDS-related workflows)\n- Clinical Quality Measures (10 CQMs certified)\n\n**Supported Terminologies** (per Medigy listing)\n- ICD-9, ICD-10, SNOMED CT, LOINC, NDC, RxNorm, CPT, HCPCS, RadLex, MEDCIN\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on the evidence gathered, ChartEasy stores or manages the following types of data:\n\n**Clinical data confirmed by product documentation:**\n- Patient demographics (received from facility EHR integrations)\n- ADT (admission/discharge/transfer) records (from facility integrations)\n- Physician progress notes and encounter documentation\n- Medication lists and reconciliation data\n- Vital signs (both manual and from RPM devices)\n- Lab results (from laboratory integrations)\n- Diagnoses (received from facility EHR, also managed internally)\n- Implantable device information (implied by (a)(14) certification)\n- Clinical decision support alerts and risk predictions (ProphEasy RTH scores)\n- Care plans (CCM care plans, accessible via portal)\n- Scheduling data (visit scheduling per regulatory requirements)\n- Patient portal access logs and patient-generated data\n\n**Clinical messaging data:**\n- ChatEasy secure messages between Theoria clinicians and facility nursing staff\n- Alert notifications for abnormal vitals\n\n**RPM device data:**\n- Heart rate, respiration rate, motion, presence, blood oxygen saturation readings\n- Continuous monitoring streams from RPM devices\n\n**What is unclear or not mentioned:**\n- **Billing/claims**: The website does not explicitly describe billing or claims management functionality within ChartEasy. However, CPT and HCPCS terminologies are listed as supported, and Theoria operates as a physician group that bills Medicare (fee-for-service and value-based). It is unclear whether billing is handled within ChartEasy or through a separate billing system.\n- **E-prescribing**: Despite medication management being a core feature, explicit e-prescribing (Surescripts integration) is not mentioned on the website. However, (a)(1) CPOE certification and RxNorm/NDC terminology support suggest prescribing workflows exist.\n- **Imaging results**: Integration with \"imaging companies\" is mentioned but details are sparse.\n- **Referral management**: Not described.\n- **Quality reporting/MDS data**: While regulatory compliance is emphasized and CQMs are certified, explicit MDS (Minimum Data Set) data management is not described — MDS is typically the facility's responsibility, not the attending physician's.\n- **Historical claims data**: Theoria references having \"historical claims data\" for ACO REACH analytics, but it's unclear if this is stored in ChartEasy or a separate analytics platform.\n\n---\n","numLines":151,"startLine":1,"totalLines":151}}}

text-justify font-main text-lg font-normal\">Theoria Medical ChartEasy™ is an ONC certified electronic health record (EHR) specifically designed for the post-acute and primary segment of care. ChartEasy™ is a secure, HIPAA compliant, cloud-based platform supported for web and iOS applications to meet the needs of all users. Theoria&#x27;s EHR is designed to maximize provider efficiency and to ensure continuity of care and health equity for patients being cared for in skilled nursing facilities, home health settings or by their primary care physician. Theoria&#x27;s technology team has self-developed and certified this software, optimized directly for its provider group, with maximized interoperability and integrations between facility partner EHRs and laboratory partner LIMS platforms.<br/><br/>This Health IT Module is compliant with the ONC Certification Criteria for Health IT and has been certified by an ONC-ACB in accordance with the applicable certification criteria adopted by the Secretary of Health and Human Services. Accordance with ONC Health IT Certification Criterion 170.315(b)(10)</strong><p class=\"mt-5 px-5 text-justify\">Theoria Medical hereby attests and confirms its commitment to enhancing patient access to their Electronic Health Information (EHI). Our Electronic Health Record system, ChartEasy™, is designed in alignment with the ONC Health IT Certification criterion 170.315(b)(10) pertaining to EHI Export.<br/><br/>Patients can readily export their EHI in the following ways:<br/><br/>1. Direct Patient Access via ChartEasy Patient Portal: Theoria offers patients direct access to their EHI via the ChartEasy Patient Portal. This portal is designed to be user-friendly and secure, ensuring that patients can conveniently retrieve their information whenever needed. Records may be exported as both PDF and CCDA format.<br/><br/>Web: <a href=\"https://patient-portal.charteasy.com/\" target=\"_blank\" class=\"text-blue-600\">https://patient-portal.charteasy.com/</a><br/><br/>iOS App: <a href=\"https://apps.apple.com/us/app/charteasy-patient-portal/id1564972475\" target=\"_blank\" class=\"text-blue-600 overflow-auto\">https://apps.apple.com/us/app/charteasy-patient-portal/id1564972475</a> <br/><br/>2. Request to Theoria Medical Records Team: In instances where further assistance or specific record retrieval is required, patients may forward their request to Theoria&#x27;s dedicated medical records team. Please send all such inquiries to: records@theoriamedical.com. Records may be exported as both PDF and CCDA format. <br/><br/>Theoria Medical takes pride in its unwavering dedication to patient privacy, security, and transparency. We continue to strive for excellence and adherence to standards that benefit both healthcare professionals and patients. <br/><br/>Should you have any questions or require further information, please don’t hesitate to reach out to our team.</p></li><li><strong>Intervention Risk Management</strong><p class=\"mt-5 px-5 text-justify\">Theoria Medical employs predictive models for our primary care practice to aid clinical decision-making, and we apply the same intervention risk managements for all of our predictive DSI models. We apply a risk analysis framework to assess validity, reliability, and fairness of our models, and our risk mitigation strategies included using real world data and direct clinician examinations to prevent any unwarranted bias or inaccuracies impacting the results. Our Electronic Health Record system, ChartEasy™, is designed in alignment with the ONC Health IT Certification criterion 170.315(b)(10) pertaining to EHI Export.\"\n    uid=1_82 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_83 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_84 StaticText \"Patients can readily export their EHI in the following ways:\"\n    uid=1_85 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_86 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_87 StaticText \"1. Direct Patient Access via ChartEasy Patient Portal: Theoria offers patients direct access to their EHI via the ChartEasy Patient Portal. This portal is designed to be user-friendly and secure, ensuring that patients can conveniently retrieve their information whenever needed. Records may be exported as both PDF and CCDA format.\"\n    uid=1_88 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_89 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_90 StaticText \"Web: \"\n    uid=1_91 link \"https://patient-portal.charteasy.com/\" url=\"https://patient-portal.charteasy.com/\"\n      uid=1_92 StaticText \"https://patient-portal.charteasy.com/\"\n    uid=1_93 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_94 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_95 StaticText \"iOS App: \"\n    uid=1_96 link \"https://apps.apple.com/us/app/charteasy-patient-portal/id1564972475\" url=\"https://apps.apple.com/us/app/charteasy-patient-portal/id1564972475\"\n      uid=1_97 StaticText \"https://apps.apple.com/us/app/charteasy-patient-portal/id1564972475\"\n    uid=1_98 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_99 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_100 StaticText \"2. Request to Theoria Medical Records Team: In instances where further assistance or specific record retrieval is required, patients may forward their request to Theoria's dedicated medical records team. Please send all such inquiries to: records@theoriamedical.com. Records may be exported as both PDF and CCDA format.\"\n    uid=1_101 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_102 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_103 StaticText \"Theoria Medical takes pride in its unwavering dedication to patient privacy, security, and transparency. We continue to strive for excellence and adherence to standards that benefit both healthcare professionals and patients.\"\n    uid=1_104 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_105 LineBreak \"\n\"\n    uid=1_106 StaticText \"Should you have any questions or require further information, please don’t hesitate to reach out to our team.\"\n    uid=1_107 StaticText \"Intervention Risk Management\"\n    uid=1_108 StaticText \"Theoria Medical employs predictive models for our primary care practice to aid clinical decision-making, and we apply the same intervention risk managements for all of our predictive DSI models. We apply a risk analysis framework to assess validity, reliability, and fairness of our models, and our risk mitigation strategies included using real world data and direct clinician examinations to prevent any unwarranted bias or inaccuracies impacting the results. Our Theoria Medical DSI committee provides governance and is tasked to evaluate potential risks in our models.\"\n    uid=1_109 image \"Theoria Medical logo\" url=\"https://theoriamedical.com/logo-blue.svg\"\n    uid=1_110 StaticText \"Theoria Medical is a leader in tech-enabled, value-\"\n    uid=1_111 StaticText \"based primary care. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_018mzqraWePvjTASmYqCVFZ7","type":"tool_result","content":" Theoria Medical™ \n window.dataLayer = window.dataLayer || [];\n function gtag(){dataLayer.push(arguments);}\n gtag('js', new Date());\n gtag('config', 'G-02BXCMK9NX', {\n page_path: window.location.pathname,\n });\n Partner With Us Compliance and Privacy Compliance Program At Theoria Medical, fostering a culture of integrity and ethical excellence is more than a commitment—it&#x27;s the essence of our identity. Our comprehensive compliance program embodies our core principles of honesty, ethical behavior, and transparency while ensuring adherence to all applicable laws, regulations, and policies. Our ethical commitments are embedded in every facet of our operations.  Theoria Medical rigorously trains, enforces and institutionalizes an ethical approach to healthcare, setting new benchmarks in ethical healthcare delivery. Retaliation-Free Reporting Your courage to speak up is valued and protected. Our dedicated hotline is more than just a number—it&#x27;s a safe channel for you to express concerns and report issues, knowing your identity will be guarded with the utmost confidentiality. We are committed to creating an environment where open communication is not just encouraged but safeguarded. We stand firmly against any form of retaliation. Reporting a concern in good faith brings no risk to you; it only helps us uphold our high standards of integrity and ethical conduct. Your willingness to come forward is essential to maintaining the trust and safety of our entire community. How to Report If you have any questions or compliance-related concerns, you may: Speak to your supervisor Contact the Compliance Department at compliance@theoriamedical.com If you are a vendor/contractor and would like a copy of our Code of Conduct, please email compliance@theoriamedical.com Report compliance concerns anonymously by visiting theoriamedicalcompliance.com or by calling the Compliance Hotline at 1-(888)-212-4171. Privacy Program At Theoria Medical, we consider patient privacy to be a critical component of the healthcare services we offer. The Theoria Medical Privacy Program focuses on developing and implementing policies and safeguards designed to ensure the confidentiality of our patients&#x27; information. Interested in understanding more about how we safeguard your information? Click here for our Privacy Policy. If you have a privacy concern: Report the concern to the Compliance Hotline at 1-(888)-212-4171. Transparency in Coverage Compliance Notice In accordance with the federal Transparency in Coverage Final Rule, Theoria Medical provides public access to Machine-Readable Files (MRFs) containing negotiated rates for covered items and services between health plans and in-network providers, as well as historical out-of-network allowed amounts. These files are intended for use by researchers, regulators, and application developers and are not designed for member-friendly navigation. Access the MRFs: here Theoria Medical is a leader in tech-enabled, value- based primary care. Theoria is revolutionizing healthcare for the senior living  communities nationwide. Here are the key findings:\n\n## ChartEasy and b(10) EHI Export\n\nTheoria Medical ChartEasy™ is an ONC certified electronic health record (EHR) specifically designed for the post-acute and primary segment of care. ChartEasy™ is designed in alignment with the ONC Health IT Certification criterion 170.315(b)(10) pertaining to EHI Export. Records may be exported as both PDF and CCDA format.\n\n## About 170.315(b)(10) Electronic Health Information Export\n\nThe documentation for the export format consists of information on the structure and syntax for how the EHI will be exported by the product such as, for example, Consolidated-Clinical Document Architecture (C-CDA) document(s) or data dictionary for comma separated values (csv) file(s).\n\nThe developer's clinical EHI export format should be made publicly available via a hyperlink as part of certification to the criterion, including keeping the hyperlink up-to-date with the current export format. Similar to the API documentation, this link will also be made available on the Certified Health IT Product List (CHPL).\n\n## Data Dictionary and Export Formats\n\nVarious EHI export implementations use different formats. The (b)(10) Data Dictionary provides information about the data included in each of the tables in the export. The EHI Export process generates CSV files, PDF files, and a folder per patient that are presented as a compressed zip file.\n\n\nREMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"0a684cb1-23e0-4dc9-b119-21c3f9eca41e","uuid":"cff3270c-6357-4e9e-8adc-199f7e006cd0","tool_use_result":{"query":"\"ChartEasy\" \"b(10)\" OR \"EHI export\" OR \"data dictionary\" OR \"electronic health information export\"","results":[{"tool_use_id":"srvtoolu_01MjBL2e3kqk95UDtApRJsSo","content":[{"title":"170.315(b)(10) Electronic Health Information export","url":"https://www.healthit.gov/test-method/electronic-health-information-export"},{"title":"ChartEasy ONC Certification","url":"https://theoriamedical.com/ehr-certificate"},{"title":"(b)(10) Electronic Health Information Export - {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Aftf5Vm8Yf4TRxLUnbYmsw","type":"tool_result","content":"# ChartEasy Patient Portal - Key Information\n\n## App Details\n- **Current Version:** 2.0.7 (released December 15, 2025)\n- **Developer:** Theoria Medical pllc\n- **Size:** 28.3 MB\n- **Minimum Requirements:** iOS 12.3 or later\n- **Age Rating:** 16+\n- **Cost:** Free\n\n## Core Features\nThe application provides patients with direct access to their health information through several key capabilities:\n\n**Health Record Access:**\nThe app allows users to \"view, download, and transmit your health records\" through a secure portal developed by Theoria Medical for their proprietary ChartEasy™ electronic health records platform.\n\n**Specific Data Access Points:**\n- Real-time access to lab results and vital signs\n- Current medication lists\n- Chronic Care Management (CCM) program plans (when enrolled)\n- Signed encounter records (added in version 2.0.4)\n\n**Data Sharing & Export:**\nUsers enjoy \"complete and secure access to your personal records while also being able to allow...authorized representatives...access your records,\" plus the ability to \"transmit your information to whomever you want, including other healthcare providers.\"\n\n## Recent Updates\nRecent versions have focused on security enhancements and usability improvements, including password reset reminders and patient detail synchronization features."}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"0a684cb1-23e0-4dc9-b119-21c3f9eca41e","uuid":"107f0f17-aa53-4c9c-a05f-b4438a22ecc0","tool_use_result":{"bytes":400823,"code":200,"codeText":"OK","result":"# ChartEasy Patient Portal - Key Information\n\n## App Details\n- **Current Version:** 2.0.7 (released December 15, 2025)\n- **Developer:** Theoria Medical pllc\n- **Size:** 28.3 MB\n- **Minimum Requirements:** iOS 12.3 or later\n- **Age Rating:** 16+\n- **Cost:** Free\n\n## Core Features\nThe application provides patients with direct access to their health information through several key capabilities:\n\n**Health Record Access:**\nThe app allows users to \"view, download, and transmit your health records\" through a secure portal developed by Theoria Medical for their proprietary ChartEasy™ electronic health records platform.\n\n**Specific Data Access Points:**\n- Real-time access to lab results and vital signs\n- Current medication lists\n- Chronic Care Management (CCM) program plans (when enrolled)\n- Signed encounter records (added in version 2.0.4)\n\n**Data Sharing & Export:**\nUsers enjoy \"complete and secure access to your personal records while also being able to allow...authorized representatives...access your records,\" plus the ability to \"transmit your information to whomever you want, including other healthcare providers.\"\n\n## Recent Updates\nRecent versions have focused on security enhancements and usability improvements, including password reset reminders and patient detail synchronization features.","durationMs":4826,"url":"https://apps.apple.com/us/app/charteasy-patient-portal/id1564972475"}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-6","id":"msg_01T7fBoELsX5fjJqQfSEPRXa","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01EdgaTVN1qDKhcjbk2wMdw8","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/jmandel/hobby/ehi-export-analysis/results/theoria-medical-pllc--charteasy/ehi-export-report.md","content":"# Theoria Medical, PLLC — EHI Export Documentation\n\nCollected: 2026-02-15\n\n## Source\n- Registered URL: https://theoriamedical.com/ehr-certificate\n- CHPL ID: 11542\n- Product: ChartEasy™ v1.5\n- Certification Date: 2024-12-04\n\n## Navigation Journal\n\n### Step 1: Probe the registered URL\n```bash\ncurl -sI -L \"https://theoriamedical.com/ehr-certificate\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n```\nReturned HTTP 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8`, powered by Next.js. No redirects.\n\n### Step 2: Download and examine the page\n```bash\ncurl -sL \"https://theoriamedical.com/ehr-certificate\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o ehr-certificate-page.html\n```\n16,621 bytes. Static HTML rendered by Next.js. The page contains:\n- ONC Certification overview text\n- Certification details (developer, date, product, CHPL number)\n- Tab buttons showing 34 certification criteria and 10 CQMs\n- Real-World Testing Plans and Reports (6 PDF links, all regulatory filings)\n- **EHI Export (b)(10) section** — a text-only attestation statement\n- Intervention Risk Management section (about predictive models)\n\n### Step 3: Search for downloadable documentation\n```bash\ngrep -oiE 'href=\"[^\"]*\\.(pdf|zip|xlsx|xls|csv|json|doc|docx|yaml|yml)[^\"]*\"' /tmp/theoria-page.html\n```\nFound 6 PDF links — all are Real-World Testing Plans/Reports, not EHI export documentation:\n- `TheorialMedical_Real_World_Test_Plan_CY2023_22Nov2022.pdf`\n- `TheorialMedical_Real_World_Test_Plan_CY2024_19Oct2023.pdf`\n- `TheoriaMedical_Real_World_Test_Results_CY2023_26Jan2024.pdf`\n- `TheoriaMedical_Real_World_Test_Results_CY2024_26Feb2025.pdf`\n- `TheorialMedical_Real_World_Test_Plan_CY2025_07Oct2024.pdf`\n- `TheoriaMedical_Real_World_Test_Results_CY2025_03Feb2026.pdf`\n\nNo EHI export data dictionaries, schemas, format specs, or downloadable export documentation found.\n\n### Step 4: Extract the (b)(10) statement\nThe full text of the EHI export section:\n\n> **Support for EHI Export in Accordance with ONC Health IT Certification Criterion 170.315(b)(10)**\n>\n> Theoria Medical hereby attests and confirms its commitment to enhancing patient access to their Electronic Health Information (EHI). Our Electronic Health Record system, ChartEasy™, is designed in alignment with the ONC Health IT Certification criterion 170.315(b)(10) pertaining to EHI Export.\n>\n> Patients can readily export their EHI in the following ways:\n>\n> 1. Direct Patient Access via ChartEasy Patient Portal: Theoria offers patients direct access to their EHI via the ChartEasy Patient Portal. This portal is designed to be user-friendly and secure, ensuring that patients can conveniently retrieve their information whenever needed. Records may be exported as both PDF and CCDA format.\n>\n> Web: https://patient-portal.charteasy.com/\n> iOS App: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/charteasy-patient-portal/id1564972475\n>\n> 2. Request to Theoria Medical Records Team: In instances where further assistance or specific record retrieval is required, patients may forward their request to Theoria's dedicated medical records team. Please send all such inquiries to: records@theoriamedical.com. Records may be exported as both PDF and CCDA format.\n>\n> Theoria Medical takes pride in its unwavering dedication to patient privacy, security, and transparency. We continue to strive for excellence and adherence to standards that benefit both healthcare professionals and patients.\n\n### Step 5: Check the patient portal\n```bash\ncurl -sI \"https://patient-portal.charteasy.com/\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0'\n```\nReturned HTTP 200. The portal is a Flutter web application (v2.0.8) requiring login. The landing page describes four features:\n1. Access Chronic Care Management Plan\n2. View Lab and Imaging Results\n3. View Medication Lists\n4. **Download and Transmit your records** — \"complete and full access to your personal records while also being able to allow any other authorized representatives you choose to have access to your records, or simply use the portal to transmit your information to whomever you want, including other healthcare providers.\"\n\nNo public documentation about export format, CCDA structure, or data dictionary is accessible without logging in.\n\n### Step 6: Check the iOS App Store listing\nThe ChartEasy Patient Portal iOS app (v2.0.7, released December 15, 2025) describes:\n- View, download, and transmit health records\n- Real-time access to lab results and vital signs\n- Current medication lists\n- CCM care plans\n- Signed encounter records (added in v2.0.4)\n- Ability to share records with authorized representatives and other providers\n\nNo additional detail about export format or data dictionary.\n\n### Step 7: Check the developer portal\nThe search results reference a FHIR API developer portal at `developer.charteasy.com`.\n```bash\ncurl -sI -L \"https://developer.charteasy.com/\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' --max-time 15\n```\nConnection timed out (curl exit code 28). The site appears to be down or unreachable. No Wayback Machine captures exist for this domain. This portal is for the (g)(10) FHIR API, not the (b)(10) EHI export, but I investigated it in case it contained relevant documentation.\n\n### Step 8: Search for alternative documentation locations\n- Probed common paths on theoriamedical.com: `/ehi`, `/ehi-export`, `/interoperability`, `/fhir`, `/api`, `/developer`, `/onc`, `/b10` — all returned 404.\n- Checked sitemap.xml — returned 404.\n- Probed for undiscovered PDFs at `/pdf/ehi*.pdf`, `/pdf/ChartEasy*.pdf`, `/pdf/data-dictionary*.pdf`, `/pdf/export*.pdf` — all 404.\n- Checked Compliance & Privacy page (`/compliance`) — contains only compliance program info, privacy policies, and Transparency in Coverage links. No EHI export documentation.\n- Google searches for `\"charteasy\" EHI export data dictionary` — returned no results beyond the same certification page.\n\n### Step 9: Took screenshots\n- Full-page screenshot of the EHR certificate page\n- Screenshot of the patient portal login page\n\n## What Was Found\n\n**The EHI export \"documentation\" consists entirely of a brief text attestation on the ONC certification page.** There is no data dictionary, no schema, no format specification, no API documentation, no sample data, and no downloadable artifacts of any kind.\n\nThe attestation states that the EHI export mechanism is:\n1. **Patient Portal self-service** — patients log in to the ChartEasy Patient Portal and can download records in PDF and CCDA format\n2. **Records request by email** — patients email records@theoriamedical.com and receive records in PDF and CCDA format\n\nThat is the entirety of what is documented. There is:\n- **No data dictionary** describing what fields or tables are included in the export\n- **No CCDA implementation guide or profile** describing which CCDA sections, entries, or templates are used\n- **No sample exports** showing what the PDF or CCDA outputs look like\n- **No schema files** (XSD, JSON Schema, OpenAPI, etc.)\n- **No description of what \"EHI\" means** in their context — i.e., which data domains from ChartEasy are included in the export\n- **No documentation of the export process** beyond \"log in to the portal\" or \"email us\"\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nBased on the product research, ChartEasy stores:\n- Patient demographics (from facility EHR integrations)\n- ADT records (admission/discharge/transfer)\n- Physician progress notes and encounter documentation\n- Medication lists and reconciliation data\n- Vital signs (manual and RPM device data)\n- Lab results (from laboratory integrations)\n- Diagnoses\n- Implantable device information\n- Clinical decision support alerts / ProphEasy RTH predictions\n- Care plans (CCM)\n- Scheduling data\n- Secure messaging data (ChatEasy)\n- RPM device readings (heart rate, respiration, SpO2, motion, presence)\n\nThe (b)(10) attestation says records are exported as \"PDF and CCDA format\" but provides **zero documentation about which data domains are included**. Given that the export mechanism is a patient portal that mentions \"lab results, vital signs, current medications, CCM plans, and signed encounters,\" the export likely covers only the patient-portal-visible subset:\n\n**Likely covered (based on portal features):**\n- Lab results\n- Vital signs\n- Current medications\n- Signed clinical encounters/progress notes\n- CCM care plans\n\n**Likely missing or unknown:**\n- ADT records\n- Full medication reconciliation history\n- RPM device data streams (heart rate, SpO2, respiration, motion)\n- ProphEasy clinical decision support predictions\n- ChatEasy secure messaging content\n- Scheduling data\n- Historical diagnoses/problem lists (unclear if in CCDA)\n- Implantable device information\n- Billing data (if ChartEasy stores any — unclear)\n- Integration data received from facility EHRs (demographics, diagnoses, vitals)\n- Imaging reports\n\n**It is impossible to assess completeness** because no data dictionary or content specification exists.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export is stated to be **PDF and CCDA**. However:\n- There is no documentation of which CCDA document type is used (CCD, Discharge Summary, Progress Note, etc.)\n- There is no documentation of which CCDA sections and entries are populated\n- There is no CCDA implementation guide, profile, or template list\n- There is no documentation of what the PDF contains vs. what the CCDA contains\n- C-CDA is a reasonable format for clinical summaries but cannot represent all of ChartEasy's data (e.g., RPM device streams, secure messages, scheduling data, CDS predictions)\n- A CCDA export alone cannot satisfy (b)(10) requirements if ChartEasy stores data that doesn't map to standard CCDA sections — and it does (RPM data, ProphEasy predictions, ChatEasy messages)\n\nThis is a classic (g)(10)/(b)(10) confusion: the patient portal's view/download/transmit capability (which is the (e)(1) certification criterion) is being repackaged as the (b)(10) EHI export. The (e)(1) VDT capability exports a clinical summary; the (b)(10) requirement is to export **all** electronic health information in the designated record set.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n**Essentially non-existent.** The documentation consists of a ~150-word attestation statement. There is:\n- No data dictionary\n- No field-level definitions\n- No data type specifications\n- No value set documentation\n- No sample exports\n- No worked examples\n- No developer-facing documentation\n- No instructions beyond \"log into the portal\" or \"email us\"\n\nA developer could not implement an import of this data based on the documentation because there is no documentation of the data format. A patient cannot understand what is included in their export because it is not specified. A regulator cannot verify completeness because there is no data dictionary to evaluate.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\nThe documentation has no structure at all. It is a single paragraph of prose. There are no tables, no schemas, no field lists. The (b)(10) requirement explicitly calls for \"documentation describing the format of the export\" to be publicly available. This documentation falls far short of that requirement.\n\n### Critical Assessment\n\nThis is one of the weakest (b)(10) documentation implementations possible:\n\n1. **The export mechanism appears to be the patient portal (e)(1) VDT capability relabeled as (b)(10).** The certification page does not describe any separate bulk export or comprehensive EHI export mechanism.\n\n2. **PDF and CCDA cannot cover all EHI** that ChartEasy stores. RPM device data, secure messages, CDS predictions, and scheduling data have no representation in C-CDA.\n\n3. **No documentation of the export format exists.** The (b)(10) criterion requires the developer to \"make publicly accessible\" documentation \"describing the format of the export.\" A sentence saying \"PDF and CCDA format\" does not satisfy this requirement.\n\n4. **The developer portal (developer.charteasy.com) is unreachable.** Even if it contained relevant FHIR API documentation, that would be (g)(10) documentation, not (b)(10).\n\n5. **Context:** Theoria Medical is a physician practice that built ChartEasy for internal use, not a traditional EHR vendor. The product was certified very recently (December 2024). This may explain the minimal documentation — the certification was obtained for compliance purposes, and the documentation requirements may not have been fully understood or prioritized.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://theoriamedical.com/ehr-certificate\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (static HTML via curl, though screenshots confirmed via browser)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- **developer.charteasy.com**: Connection times out. No Wayback Machine captures. Would have been the FHIR API developer portal but is unreachable.\n- **Patient portal**: Requires login. No public-facing export documentation.\n- **No alternative documentation paths**: Exhaustively probed common paths, searched Google, checked the compliance page. No additional EHI export documentation exists on the public site.\n- **No downloadable artifacts**: The only PDFs on the site are Real-World Testing Plans/Reports, which are regulatory filings unrelated to EHI export.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":324,"cache_read_input_tokens":62875,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":324},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"0a684cb1-23e0-4dc9-b119-21c3f9eca41e","uuid":"6f28dfac-4436-4896-aa3f-9a07ffb2472d"}

However:\n- There is no documentation of which CCDA document type is used (CCD, Discharge Summary, Progress Note, etc.)\n- There is no documentation of which CCDA sections and entries are populated\n- There is no CCDA implementation guide, profile, or template list\n- There is no documentation of what the PDF contains vs. what the CCDA contains\n- C-CDA is a reasonable format for clinical summaries but cannot represent all of ChartEasy's data (e.g., RPM device streams, secure messages, scheduling data, CDS predictions)\n- A CCDA export alone cannot satisfy (b)(10) requirements if ChartEasy stores data that doesn't map to standard CCDA sections — and it does (RPM data, ProphEasy predictions, ChatEasy messages)\n\nThis is a classic (g)(10)/(b)(10) confusion: the patient portal's view/download/transmit capability (which is the (e)(1) certification criterion) is being repackaged as the (b)(10) EHI export. The (e)(1) VDT capability exports a clinical summary; the (b)(10) requirement is to export **all** electronic health information in the designated record set.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\n**Essentially non-existent.** The documentation consists of a ~150-word attestation statement. There is:\n- No data dictionary\n- No field-level definitions\n- No data type specifications\n- No value set documentation\n- No sample exports\n- No worked examples\n- No developer-facing documentation\n- No instructions beyond \"log into the portal\" or \"email us\"\n\nA developer could not implement an import of this data based on the documentation because there is no documentation of the data format. A patient cannot understand what is included in their export because it is not specified. A regulator cannot verify completeness because there is no data dictionary to evaluate.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\nThe documentation has no structure at all. It is a single paragraph of prose. There are no tables, no schemas, no field lists. The (b)(10) requirement explicitly calls for \"documentation describing the format of the export\" to be publicly available. This documentation falls far short of that requirement.\n\n### Critical Assessment\n\nThis is one of the weakest (b)(10) documentation implementations possible:\n\n1. **The export mechanism appears to be the patient portal (e)(1) VDT capability relabeled as (b)(10).** The certification page does not describe any separate bulk export or comprehensive EHI export mechanism.\n\n2. **PDF and CCDA cannot cover all EHI** that ChartEasy stores. RPM device data, secure messages, CDS predictions, and scheduling data have no representation in C-CDA.\n\n3. **No documentation of the export format exists.** The (b)(10) criterion requires the developer to \"make publicly accessible\" documentation \"describing the format of the export.\" A sentence saying \"PDF and CCDA format\" does not satisfy this requirement.\n\n4. **The developer portal (developer.charteasy.com) is unreachable.** Even if it contained relevant FHIR API documentation, that would be (g)(10) documentation, not (b)(10).\n\n5. **Context:** Theoria Medical is a physician practice that built ChartEasy for internal use, not a traditional EHR vendor. The product was certified very recently (December 2024). This may explain the minimal documentation — the certification was obtained for compliance purposes, and the documentation requirements may not have been fully understood or prioritized.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://theoriamedical.com/ehr-certificate\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (static HTML via curl, though screenshots confirmed via browser)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- **developer.charteasy.com**: Connection times out. No Wayback Machine captures. Would have been the FHIR API developer portal but is unreachable.\n- **Patient portal**: Requires login. No public-facing export documentation.\n- **No alternative documentation paths**: Exhaustively probed common paths, searched Google, checked the compliance page. No additional EHI export documentation exists on the public site.\n- **No downloadable artifacts**: The only PDFs on the site are Real-World Testing Plans/Reports, which are regulatory filings unrelated to EHI export.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null}}
